root_cause: rich.cells.chop_cells iterated the text in reverse (for character, size in reversed(characters)), building chunks from the END of the word and returning reversed strings. divide_line in rich/_wrap.py only uses len()/cell_len() of those chunks to place break offsets, so with double-width characters the chunk sizes (in characters) came out in the wrong order: a fold boundary could fall inside a 2-cell character, and the break offsets no longer matched the real text, so the tail of CJK lines was dropped (issue #3176: 'Textualは...ムワークです' loses 'ムワークです').
best_solution: Make chop_cells split left-to-right: iterate `for character in text`, start a new line when total_width + cell_width > width, else append; return [''.join(line) for line in lines]. The gold PR also renamed max_size->width, removed the unused `position` arg (call site becomes chop_cells(word, width=width)), and rewrote divide_line with clearer names (remaining_space, cell_offset, break_positions) plus docstrings, but divide_line's logic is semantically unchanged. Verified locally: the single-line change `reversed(characters)` -> `characters` in cells.py makes all 114 tests in tests/test_cells.py + tests/test_text.py pass (base: 4 fail). Reasoning path from the statement: 'fold location sat within a double-width character' -> the fold helper that divide_line calls is chop_cells -> its docstring literally says 'returning the characters in reverse order' -> chunk from the start instead.
acceptable_alternatives: Any chop_cells that returns forward-order chunks each <= width cells, greedy from the start, keeping the old call signature (tests call chop_cells(text, 3) positionally, so keeping max_size/position is fine as long as position=0 at the call site).

'; plus new wrap tests (long word followed by words, word of full line length before long word, multiple consecutive spaces, leading/trailing whitespace) that already pass at base, and pre-existing test_wrap_long*, test_wrap_cjk*, test_wrap_long_words_justify_left must keep passing.
locating_signals: Statement (PR description) says 'wrapping logic', 'fold location sat within a double-width character', 'CJK characters disappearing'. Neither chop_cells nor divide_line is named; 'wrap'/'fold' leads to rich/_wrap.py:divide_line, whose fold branch calls chop_cells(word, max_size=width, position=0); chop_cells's docstring 'returning the characters in reverse order' is the tell. Linked issue #3176 has concrete repros (Console(width=20).print('アプリケーションは1670万色を使用でき') drops the 7).
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4 (193s/73 calls): left chop_cells reversed and instead reversed its output at the call site (loop_last(chopped_words[::-1])), so the short remainder chunk came first and break offsets shifted; 13 failures including 9 pre-existing wrap tests; also committed repro.py/test_repro.py. v6 (76s/52 calls): added a branch in chop_cells for an empty current line that never fires in practice, still reverse iteration; no-op, same 4 failures as base (3 chop_cells tests + test_wrap_cjk_mixed). v7 (89s/45 calls): set line_position=width in divide_line's non-last fold branch, which is overwritten on the last chunk; no-op, same 4 failures. v8 (108s/63 calls): closest - correctly changed chop_cells to forward iteration (all chop_cells tests and test_wrap_cjk_mixed pass) but also changed the call to position=line_position, so the first folded chunk was sized to the leftover space on the current line while divide_line still inserts a break before it; 7 pre-existing/new long-word wrap tests failed (e.g. justify_left gives '1   ' instead of '1234'). Dropping that one extra edit would have passed all 114 (verified).
generalizable_lesson: Fix the helper at its root and keep the fix minimal: when a helper's own docstring or loop admits an odd behavior (reverse order, off-by-position), correct the helper instead of compensating at the call site, and do not alter other call-site arguments. Before finishing, run the existing test file for the module you touched (here tests/test_text.py already had test_wrap_long* that v4 and v8 broke) and add a round-trip invariant check (''.join(chunks) == input, each chunk width <= limit) with mixed single/double-width input.
